newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: CALLS FOR PM TO SPEAK OUT & HANSON TO RESIGN
Union, indigenous, and ethnic groups are calling for the resignation of Federal Independent MP Pauline Hanson.
Launching an anti-racism campaign in Brisbane today, the groups want an apology from Ms Hanson, and have chastised the Prime Minister over his lack of vigour in the debate.
Indigenous group spokesman, Denis Borbongie, says the Prime Minister has been irresponsible in allowing racism to rear its ugly head.
Mr Borbongie says under Labor's policies of multiculturalism such overt acts of racism weren't tolerated.
HANSON CALLS FOR REFERENDUM ON RACIAL INTOLERANCE
Federal Independent MP, Pauline Hanson, says she was absent during yesterday afternoon's parliamentary debate on a bipartisan motion denouncing racial intolerance, due to a prior engagement.
Ms Hanson says she'd arranged to visit the Melbourne Wholesale Fruit and Vegetable Markets at five o'clock this morning.
She says she received a warm welcome, far different from her experience in Parliament House.
Ms Hanson says the Government and Opposition have had their say, but she's called for a referendum to settle the matter.
The member for Oxley says yesterday's motion is only the start of the debate, and the final say will be given to mainstream Australians at the next election.
KENNETT WANTS TO CHANGE HANSON'S MIND
The Victorian Premier says he wants to meet with Pauline Hanson to get her to retract her comments against Asian immigration because of the effect they may have on the 2000 Olympics.
Jeff Kennett says Ms Hanson's views could lead to some countries boycotting the Sydney Olympics, and damage Melbourne's bid for the Commonwealth Games.
Mr Kennett says she should reconsider her agenda because it's out of touch, and very dangerous.
He says if Ms Hanson continues on this track, she'll damage Australia's trade potential in Asia, and that will eventually mean job losses in Australia.
BORBIDGE BRIEFS GOVERNOR
Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge has briefed Governor Leneen Forde on the outcome of today's no-confidence vote in his Government.
The motion, moved by the Opposition, was defeated after Gladstone Independent, Liz Cunningham, joined the Government in voting against it.
Labor brought on the motion after the resignation of Kenneth Carruthers QC this week.
Mr Carruthers claimed the independence of his inquiry into pre-election deals had been compromised, because the Government has given a judicial review into the C-J-C powers over his inquiry.
FEDERAL PARLIAMENT ERUPTS IN FEDERAL PARLIAMENT
One Labor front bencher has been suspended from Federal Parliament, and the debate on the anti-euthanasia bill postponed, after raucous exchanges in the House.
The debate on the Kevin Andrews Bill to override the Northern Territory's voluntary euthanasia law will resume next Wednesday.
The uproar followed resumption of the debate in a side chamber of the Parliament.
Labor MP Steven Smith called for the debate to be moved back into the main chamber, a move backed by Labor's Mark Latham who was ejected after the dissent motion escalated into a shouting match.
PM TAKES CREDIT FOR LOWER MORTGAGE PAYMENTS
The Prime Minister says Australian mortgage holders are paying more than one hundred dollars less per month on home-loans since the Coaltion has come to power.
John Howard says home-loan mortgage rates are at the lowest level for over 20 years, which is good news for battlers.
The National Australia Bank and FAI First Mortgage are the latest financial institutions to cut interest rates.
The NAB is reducing rates on one to five year fixed loans by up to one per cent, with FAI lowering two, three and five year rates by just over half a per cent.
DEFENCE AGREEMENT REAFFIRMED
An agreement between Australia and Singapore has called for the enhancement of the Five Power Defence Arrangement.
The communique, produced after two days of Ministerial talks in Canberra, says Australia, New Zealand and Britain should cooperate in the defence of Malaysia and Singapore.
Foreign Minister, Alexander Downer, says the arrangement does not impact on Australia's security arrangement with Indonesia.
ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS WORKING AS PROSTITUTES
Immigration and Customs officials in Perth have arrested nine illegal immigrants working as prostitutes.
The women, believed to be South Africans from Capetown, have been arrested following raids on premises in the port city of Fremantle and the inner suburb of Como.
The ABC has been told the sex racket has been in existence for some time and the women are not the first group of South Africans to arrive in Perth to set up brothels.
They entered Australia on visitor visas, but have been working on the Fremantle wharf, visiting Japanese tuna boats.
It's also understood some of the women have been the subject of complaints after trying to solicit customers at Perth's Burswood Casino.
Officials are still trying to locate the men believe to be responsible for setting up the racket.
NEW BLOOD BANK IN BRISBANE
Brisbane's Mater Mothers' Hospital has set up a new blood bank to specialise in the blood of new born babies.
The bank keeps the umbilical cord blood which was previously discarded.
Director of Haematology, Dr Kerry Taylor, says the blood of a new born can do away with the need to obtain an exact donor match to fight disorders like leukaemia.
He says the bank will be especially helpful for patients of ethnic origin who aren't well represented on bone marrow registries.
SOLAR RACE TO STAY IN AUSTRALIA
The South Australian Government has ended speculation about the future of the World Solar Challenge, by buying the rights to the race for 300-thousand dollars.
Premier, Dean Brown, says bids for the race had also been made from the United States and Europe.
He says the purchase of the rights means that Adelaide will continue to receive international media attention.
Mr Brown hopes the solar race can be staged every two years, rather than three.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
